cases.title: Account markup precedence: account, then account group, then default
cases.objective: The most specific account markup plan applies, and each less specific level is used only when the more specific one is absent.

steps.action: Configure a default USD markup of 2%, an account-group markup of 1.5% for group G, and an account markup of 1% for account A in G.
Run the EOD accrual for account A with a $50,000 USD loan.
steps.expectedResult: The account markup of 1% is used.

steps.action: Remove the account markup and run the accrual again.
steps.expectedResult: The group markup of 1.5% is used.

steps.action: Remove the group markup and run the accrual again.
steps.expectedResult: The default markup of 2% is used.

cases.title: Instrument markup precedence falls through to 0%

steps.action: Define a 5% markup on instrument US1, a 2% instrument-group markup on a group containing US1 and US2, and nothing for US3.
Run the EOD accrual with $10,000 loaned on each of US1, US2 and US3 (USD, 360 days).
steps.expectedResult: Instrument markup is $1.39 for US1 (5%), $0.56 for US2 (2%) and $0.00 for US3.

cases.title: Daily accrual, Day 1 of the source example: USD $40.12 and GBP £3.16
cases.objective: Reproduce the source's Day 1 figures. The source's own arithmetic gives $27.62 where the formula yields $27.61 and £0.83 where it yields £0.82; the rounding rule is an open question on the page and the expected values below are the source's.

steps.action: Set USD base 5.1% / 360 days, GBP base 5.5% / 365 days, USD account tiers 2.5% up to $100k and 2% above, GBP account markup 3%, instrument markups US1 5%, US2 0%, GB1 3%.
Open positions with utilized margin US1 $90,000, US2 $50,000, GB1 £10,000, then run EOD.
steps.expectedResult: USD accrual $40.12 (base and account $27.62 at Tier 2, instrument $12.50); GBP accrual £3.16 (£2.33 + £0.83). Both are added to the account's ledger in their currency.

cases.title: Loan amount for a day is start-of-day plus opened, and ignores intra-day reductions

steps.action: Day 1: open a position with a $10,000 loan; run EOD.
steps.expectedResult: Loan amount for the day is $10,000.

steps.action: Day 3: close part of the position, reducing the loan to $7,000, and open $5,000 more on the same instrument; run EOD.
steps.expectedResult: Loan amount for the day is $15,000 ($10,000 SOD + $5,000 opened).

steps.action: Day 4: close the whole position; run EOD.
steps.expectedResult: Loan amount for the day is $15,000; Day 5 is $0.

cases.title: Monthly posting sums unprocessed accruals into one debit and marks them processed

steps.action: Accrue $40.12, $42.09 and $12.67 USD and £3.16 × 3 GBP across a month.
Advance to 00:00:00 on the first trading day of the next month.
steps.expectedResult: A debit of $94.88 impacts Available Cash on the USD wallet and a debit of £9.48 on the GBP wallet.
Nothing is posted; all six accruals are marked processed.

cases.title: Withdrawal triggers an immediate accrual and posting

steps.action: Mid-month, with unprocessed accruals and an open $60,000 USD loan, the client withdraws money.
steps.expectedResult: An accrual for today is computed on the current margin loan amount, posted as a debit to Available Cash together with the unprocessed accruals, and all of them are marked processed.

plan.name: Margin interest
plan.description: Verifies the margin interest calculation, accrual and posting against the Margin interest specification.
plan.scopeText: Base rate and day count per currency; account markup levels and precedence; instrument markup precedence; daily accrual formula and ledger; loan amount per day; monthly posting; event-driven posting.
plan.outOfScopeText: The base rate feeds themselves (SOFR, ESTR, SONIA are marked unconfirmed in the source); rounding policy until answered; loan amounts above the top configured tier.
